headlines.title: Anthropic falls below IPO price as Nvidia gives back gains
headlines.summary: In this edition of Sozzi Unleashed: At The Close, Brian Sozzi sorts through "reality trading" as Nvidia slides nearly 7% after Monday's 31% surge and Anthropic falls below its $83 IPO price less than a week after the biggest offering in history. GCG Advisory Partners' Bill Gunderson makes the case that Nvidia is the cheapest growth stock in the market at nine times forward earnings and names Nvidia and Eli Lilly as his top picks for 2027. Brian breaks down Dell's blowout quarter and $132 billion AI backlog, and HPE CEO Antonio Neri joins to explain the company's raised outlook, why it refuses to finance neoclouds, and whether server margins have peaked. Brian closes by arguing the AI trade is reaching consumers' wallets, pointing to Best Buy's strongest comparable sales growth in five years.

headlines.title: Does PepsiCo (PEP) Change Its Long Term Case With Its Efficiency Reset?
headlines.summary: PepsiCo (NasdaqGS:PEP) outlined a broad efficiency plan that trims its product portfolio and targets higher operational margins. The company signed a new 10 year beverage and snacks partnership with Hyatt Hotels, covering more than 700 U.S. properties. Management tied these moves to ongoing sustainability commitments and continued focus on Frito Lay as a key growth platform.

headlines.title: PETA, PepsiCo shareholders call out animal abuse across its supply chain
headlines.summary: The activist group is urging PepsiCo to be more transparent about the treatment of animals across its supply chain, especially in India, and honor its animal welfare policies.

headlines.title: Is PepsiCo Sacrificing Pricing Power to Regain Snack Volumes?
headlines.summary: PEP's affordability push is reviving snack volumes and market share, but mounting margin pressure raises questions about sustainable growth and pricing power.

description: PepsiCo, Inc. engages in the manufacture, marketing, distribution, and sale of various beverages and convenient foods worldwide. The company operates through six segments: PepsiCo Foods North America; PepsiCo Beverages North America; International Beverages Franchise; Europe, Middle East and Africa; Latin America Foods; and Asia Pacific Foods. It offers cereals, chips, dips, granola bars, oatmeal, pasta, rice, and syrups and mixes; refrigerated dips and spreads; beverage concentrates, fountain syrups, and finished goods; and ready-to-drink tea and coffee products. The company also provides SodaStream sparkling water makers and related products, as well as various dairy products under the Agusha, Chudo, and Domik v Derevne brands. It serves wholesale and other distributors, foodservice customers, grocery stores, drug stores, convenience stores, discount/dollar stores, mass merchandisers, membership stores, hard discounters, e-commerce retailers and authorized independent bottlers, and others through a network of direct-store-delivery, customer warehouse, and distributor networks, as well as directly to consumers through e-commerce platforms and retailers. PepsiCo, Inc. was founded in 1898 and is based in Purchase, New York.
